section_1.title: The Hook: Meet Milly the Laser Robot
section_1.content: Introduce the premise of the problem using a character-driven scenario. Explain the setup: a set of points (stars) on a flat plane and a rotating line (a laser beam).
section_1.example: Milly the Robot stands in a field of glowing stars. She holds a long laser beam that rotates clockwise. The goal is to see how the beam 'jumps' between stars.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: Pivots and Rotation
section_2.content: Review basic geometry concepts: what a pivot point is, the nature of 180-degree rotation, and how a line divides a plane into two half-planes.
section_2.example: Visualizing a see-saw: one point is the fixed center (pivot). If we rotate the see-saw 180 degrees, the 'left' side becomes the 'right' side.

section_3.title: The Core Rule: The Hand-off
section_3.content: Define the 'Windmill' movement rule. A line rotates around a pivot point until it hits another point in the set. At that exact moment, the hit point becomes the new pivot, and the rotation continues.
section_3.example: An animation of a rotating baton. As soon as the tip of the baton touches a bystander, that person grabs the center and the baton starts spinning around their hand instead.

section_4.title: The Invariant Property: The Balancing Act
section_4.content: Introduce the 'Aha!' moment: the 'Number of Points on One Side' property. Explain that as the line rotates and changes pivots, the number of points on the left side of the line remains constant.
section_4.example: Imagine 5 sheep in a field. If the laser line starts with 2 sheep on its left, no matter how many times it 'hits' a new sheep and changes pivots, there will always be exactly 2 sheep on the left side.

section_5.title: Step-by-Step Visualization (3-Point Case)
section_5.content: Walk through a full 180-degree rotation cycle using a simple triangle of points to show how the pivot moves and how the line returns to its original orientation.
section_5.example: Point A is the pivot. The line hits Point B (Pivot B). It then hits Point C (Pivot C). After 180 degrees, the line is parallel to its start position, but the 'left' and 'right' sides have swapped.

section_6.title: Conclusion: The Infinite Loop
section_6.content: Summarize the conclusion: because the number of points on each side is invariant and there are a finite number of points, the process must eventually repeat. This proves the windmill will hit every point if started correctly.
section_6.example: A final top-down view showing the 'Windmill' tracing a beautiful, symmetrical flower-like pattern as it infinitely cycles through the stars.

outline.title: Conclusion: The Infinite Loop
outline.content: Summarize the conclusion: because the number of points on each side is invariant and there are a finite number of points, the process must eventually repeat. This proves the windmill will hit every point if started correctly.
outline.example: A final top-down view showing the 'Windmill' tracing a beautiful, symmetrical flower-like pattern as it infinitely cycles through the stars.

storyboard.title: Conclusion: The Infinite Loop
lecture_lines: The invariant side-count ensures a repeating cycle.
With finite stars, the windmill hits every point.
Geometry transforms a simple rule into an infinite dance.
animations: Accelerate the animation, showing the laser quickly cycling through various stars in the set.
As the laser hits each star, it briefly glows to show it has been part of the windmill process.
Fade out the points and line to leave behind a complex, symmetric pattern of the line's history.

Color the regions on either side of the rotating line in light magenta (#FF00FF, opacity 0.2) and light green (#00FF00, opacity 0.2).

outline.content: Walk through a full 180-degree rotation cycle using a simple triangle of points to show how the pivot moves and how the line returns to its original orientation.

outline.title: The Core Rule: The Hand-off
outline.content: Define the 'Windmill' movement rule. A line rotates around a pivot point until it hits another point in the set. At that exact moment, the hit point becomes the new pivot, and the rotation continues.
outline.example: An animation of a rotating baton. As soon as the tip of the baton touches a bystander, that person grabs the center and the baton starts spinning around their hand instead.

storyboard.title: Step-by-Step Visualization (3-Point Case)
lecture_lines: Start with the laser pivoting at Point A.
It rotates and hits Point B, its new pivot.
Next, it hits Point C and continues spinning.
After 180 degrees, the line returns to Point A.
Notice how the sides have now completely swapped.
animations: Draw three stars A, B, and C in a triangular formation on the plane.
The laser starts at star A, rotates clockwise, and 'hands off' the pivot to star B.
The laser rotates from star B, hits star C, and then rotates from star C back to star A.
Show the laser line returning to its original horizontal orientation after a total rotation of 180 degrees.
Draw a faint grey dotted path (#555555) connecting A, B, and C to show the pivot's movement.

storyboard.title: The Core Rule: The Hand-off
lecture_lines: The laser rotates around its current pivot point.
It continues until it hits another star.
Instantly, that new star becomes the pivot.
The rotation continues from this new center.
This "hand-off" creates the windmill motion.
animations: Show a cyan line (#00FFFF) rotating clockwise around a yellow pivot star A (#FFFF00).
The line rotates until it makes contact with a white star B (#FFFFFF).
Star B flashes and turns yellow (#FFFF00) while Star A turns white (#FFFFFF), indicating the pivot has changed.
The cyan line continues rotating clockwise, now using Star B as its center of rotation.
Repeat the sequence: the line hits a third star C, which then becomes the new yellow pivot star.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Core Rule: The Hand-off"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- The laser rotates around its current pivot point.",
            "- It continues until it hits another star.",
            "- Instantly, that new star becomes the pivot.",
            "- The rotation continues from this new center.",
            "- This \"hand-off\" creates the windmill motion."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_CYAN = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_YELLOW = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_WHITE = "#FFFFFF"

        # Star positions on grid
        # Avoid Row A (Title) and Column 6 (Clipping)
        # B3, C4, E5
        pos_a = self.grid["C3"]
        pos_b = self.grid["B4"]
        pos_c = self.grid["E5"]

        # Stars
        star_a = Star(n=5, outer_radius=0.2, inner_radius=0.1, color=COLOR_YELLOW, fill_opacity=1)
        star_b = Star(n=5, outer_radius=0.2, inner_radius=0.1, color=COLOR_WHITE, fill_opacity=1)
        star_c = Star(n=5, outer_radius=0.2, inner_radius=0.1, color=COLOR_WHITE, fill_opacity=1)

        self.place_at_grid(star_a, "C3")
        self.place_at_grid(star_b, "B4")
        self.place_at_grid(star_c, "E5")

        # Labels
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        label_c = Text("C", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        
        # Place labels near stars (within 1 grid unit)
        self.place_at_grid(label_a, "C2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(label_b, "B3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(label_c, "E4", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Line setup
        # The line is long enough to cover the grid area
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(60 * DEGREES)
        pivot_tracker = ValueTracker(0) # 0: A, 1: B, 2: C
        
        # Line logic: must pass through the current pivot
        # We use a long line (length 8)
        line = Line(start=LEFT*4, end=RIGHT*4, color=COLOR_CYAN, stroke_width=4)
        
        def line_updater(obj):
            p_idx = int(pivot_tracker.get_value())
            if p_idx == 0:
                center = pos_a
            elif p_idx == 1:
                center = pos_b
            else:
                center = pos_c
            
            angle = angle_tracker.get_value()
            obj.set_angle(angle)
            obj.move_to(center)

        line.add_updater(line_updater)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "- The laser rotates around its current pivot point."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_CYAN)
        self.add(star_a, star_b, star_c, label_a, label_b, label_c)
        self.play(Create(line), run_time=1)
        
        # Start rotating CW
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(45 * DEGREES), run_time=1.5, rate_func=linear)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "- It continues until it hits another star."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_CYAN)
        
        # Calculate angle when line hits Star B (pos_b) from Star A (pos_a)
        # Vector AB = pos_b - pos_a
        vec_ab = pos_b - pos_a
        target_angle_ab = np.arctan2(vec_ab[1], vec_ab[0]) # approx 26.5 deg
        
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(target_angle_ab), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "- Instantly, that new star becomes the pivot."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_YELLOW)
        
        # Swap pivot to B
        self.play(
            star_a.animate.set_color(COLOR_WHITE),
            star_b.animate.set_color(COLOR_YELLOW),
            Indicate(star_b, color=COLOR_YELLOW),
            pivot_tracker.animate.set_value(1),
            run_time=1
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "- The rotation continues from this new center."
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_CYAN)
        
        # Calculate angle when line hits Star C (pos_c) from Star B (pos_b)
        # Vector BC = pos_c - pos_b
        vec_bc = pos_c - pos_b
        target_angle_bc = np.arctan2(vec_bc[1], vec_bc[0])
        # Since we rotate CW, we might need to adjust the target angle if it's "behind" the current one
        # Current target_angle_ab is ~26.5 deg. 
        # vec_bc = (4.5 - 3.5, -1.8 - 1.2) = (1.0, -3.0). Angle is arctan(-3) approx -71.5 deg.
        # Rotating CW from 26.5 to -71.5 is a decrease of ~98 degrees.
        
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(target_angle_bc), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "- This \"hand-off\" creates the windmill motion."
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_YELLOW)
        
        # Swap pivot to C
        self.play(
            star_b.animate.set_color(COLOR_WHITE),
            star_c.animate.set_color(COLOR_YELLOW),
            Indicate(star_c, color=COLOR_YELLOW),
            pivot_tracker.animate.set_value(2),
            run_time=1
        )
        
        # Rotate a bit more to show the hand-off is complete
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(target_angle_bc - 30 * DEGREES), run_time=1.5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Core Rule: The Hand-off"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- The laser rotates around its current pivot point.",
            "- It continues until it hits another star.",
            "- Instantly, that new star becomes the pivot.",
            "- The rotation continues from this new center.",
            "- This \"hand-off\" creates the windmill motion."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_CYAN = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_YELLOW = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_WHITE = "#FFFFFF"

        # Star positions on grid
        # Avoid Row A (Title) and Column 6 (Clipping)
        # B3, C4, E5
        pos_a = self.grid["C3"]
        pos_b = self.grid["B4"]
        pos_c = self.grid["E5"]

        # Stars
        star_a = Star(n=5, outer_radius=0.2, inner_radius=0.1, color=COLOR_YELLOW, fill_opacity=1)
        star_b = Star(n=5, outer_radius=0.2, inner_radius=0.1, color=COLOR_WHITE, fill_opacity=1)
        star_c = Star(n=5, outer_radius=0.2, inner_radius=0.1, color=COLOR_WHITE, fill_opacity=1)

        self.place_at_grid(star_a, "C3")
        self.place_at_grid(star_b, "B4")
        self.place_at_grid(star_c, "E5")

        # Labels
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        label_c = Text("C", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        
        # Place labels near stars (within 1 grid unit)
        self.place_at_grid(label_a, "C2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(label_b, "B3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(label_c, "E4", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Line setup
        # The line is long enough to cover the grid area
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(60 * DEGREES)
        pivot_tracker = ValueTracker(0) # 0: A, 1: B, 2: C
        
        # Line logic: must pass through the current pivot
        # We use a long line (length 8)
        line = Line(start=LEFT*4, end=RIGHT*4, color=COLOR_CYAN, stroke_width=4)
        
        def line_updater(obj):
            p_idx = int(pivot_tracker.get_value())
            if p_idx == 0:
                center = pos_a
            elif p_idx == 1:
                center = pos_b
            else:
                center = pos_c
            
            angle = angle_tracker.get_value()
            obj.set_angle(angle)
            obj.move_to(center)

        line.add_updater(line_updater)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "- The laser rotates around its current pivot point."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_CYAN)
        self.add(star_a, star_b, star_c, label_a, label_b, label_c)
        self.play(Create(line), run_time=1)
        
        # Start rotating CW
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(45 * DEGREES), run_time=1.5, rate_func=linear)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "- It continues until it hits another star."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_CYAN)
        
        # Calculate angle when line hits Star B (pos_b) from Star A (pos_a)
        # Vector AB = pos_b - pos_a
        vec_ab = pos_b - pos_a
        target_angle_ab = np.arctan2(vec_ab[1], vec_ab[0]) # approx 26.5 deg
        
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(target_angle_ab), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "- Instantly, that new star becomes the pivot."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_YELLOW)
        
        # Swap pivot to B
        self.play(
            star_a.animate.set_color(COLOR_WHITE),
            star_b.animate.set_color(COLOR_YELLOW),
            Indicate(star_b, color=COLOR_YELLOW),
            pivot_tracker.animate.set_value(1),
            run_time=1
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "- The rotation continues from this new center."
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_CYAN)
        
        # Calculate angle when line hits Star C (pos_c) from Star B (pos_b)
        # Vector BC = pos_c - pos_b
        vec_bc = pos_c - pos_b
        target_angle_bc = np.arctan2(vec_bc[1], vec_bc[0])
        # Since we rotate CW, we might need to adjust the target angle if it's "behind" the current one
        # Current target_angle_ab is ~26.5 deg. 
        # vec_bc = (4.5 - 3.5, -1.8 - 1.2) = (1.0, -3.0). Angle is arctan(-3) approx -71.5 deg.
        # Rotating CW from 26.5 to -71.5 is a decrease of ~98 degrees.
        
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(target_angle_bc), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "- This \"hand-off\" creates the windmill motion."
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_YELLOW)
        
        # Swap pivot to C
        self.play(
            star_b.animate.set_color(COLOR_WHITE),
            star_c.animate.set_color(COLOR_YELLOW),
            Indicate(star_c, color=COLOR_YELLOW),
            pivot_tracker.animate.set_value(2),
            run_time=1
        )
        
        # Rotate a bit more to show the hand-off is complete
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(target_angle_bc - 30 * DEGREES), run_time=1.5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)

            FadeIn(star_a), FadeIn(star_b), FadeIn(star_c),
            Write(label_a), Write(label_b), Write(label_c),
            FadeIn(laser)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Rotate CW to -45 degrees (hitting B)
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(color_b),
            angle_tracker.animate.set_value(-45 * DEGREES),
            run_time=2,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        # Shift pivot to B
        pivot_dot.move_to(pos_b)
        self.play(Indicate(star_b, color=color_b))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Rotate CW to -135 degrees (hitting C)

            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(color_c),
            angle_tracker.animate.set_value(-135 * DEGREES),
            run_time=2,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        # Shift pivot to C

        self.play(Indicate(star_c, color=color_c))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Rotate CW to -180 degrees (returning to Point A's line)
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            angle_tracker.animate.set_value(-180 * DEGREES),
            run_time=2,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        # Conceptually the pivot hits A again at this angle
        pivot_dot.move_to(pos_a)
        
        # Show pivot path (triangle ABC)
        path_pts = [pos_a, pos_b, pos_c, pos_a]

        self.play(Create(dashed_path))
        self.play(Indicate(star_a, color=color_a))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===

        self.place_at_grid(swap_text, "A4", scale_factor=0.8)

            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(color_swap),
            Write(swap_text),
            Indicate(laser_left, color=color_line_left),
            Indicate(laser_right, color=color_line_right)
        )

section_1.title: The Hook: Meet Milly the Laser Robot
section_1.content: Introduce the premise of the problem using a character-driven scenario. Explain the setup: a set of points (stars) on a flat plane and a rotating line (a laser beam).
section_1.example: Milly the Robot stands in a field of glowing stars. She holds a long laser beam that rotates clockwise. The goal is to see how the beam 'jumps' between stars.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: Pivots and Rotation
section_2.content: Review basic geometry concepts: what a pivot point is, the nature of 180-degree rotation, and how a line divides a plane into two half-planes.
section_2.example: Visualizing a see-saw: one point is the fixed center (pivot). If we rotate the see-saw 180 degrees, the 'left' side becomes the 'right' side.

section_3.title: The Core Rule: The Hand-off
section_3.content: Define the 'Windmill' movement rule. A line rotates around a pivot point until it hits another point in the set. At that exact moment, the hit point becomes the new pivot, and the rotation continues.
section_3.example: An animation of a rotating baton. As soon as the tip of the baton touches a bystander, that person grabs the center and the baton starts spinning around their hand instead.

section_4.title: The Invariant Property: The Balancing Act
section_4.content: Introduce the 'Aha!' moment: the 'Number of Points on One Side' property. Explain that as the line rotates and changes pivots, the number of points on the left side of the line remains constant.
section_4.example: Imagine 5 sheep in a field. If the laser line starts with 2 sheep on its left, no matter how many times it 'hits' a new sheep and changes pivots, there will always be exactly 2 sheep on the left side.

section_5.title: Step-by-Step Visualization (3-Point Case)
section_5.content: Walk through a full 180-degree rotation cycle using a simple triangle of points to show how the pivot moves and how the line returns to its original orientation.
section_5.example: Point A is the pivot. The line hits Point B (Pivot B). It then hits Point C (Pivot C). After 180 degrees, the line is parallel to its start position, but the 'left' and 'right' sides have swapped.

section_6.title: Conclusion: The Infinite Loop
section_6.content: Summarize the conclusion: because the number of points on each side is invariant and there are a finite number of points, the process must eventually repeat. This proves the windmill will hit every point if started correctly.
section_6.example: A final top-down view showing the 'Windmill' tracing a beautiful, symmetrical flower-like pattern as it infinitely cycles through the stars.

section_1.title: The Hook: Meet Milly the Laser Robot
lecture_lines: Meet Milly, a robot in a field of stars.
She holds a laser beam that rotates clockwise.
Today, we explore how this beam moves.
animations: Create a field of several small white circles (#FFFFFF) representing stars scattered randomly on a black background.
Introduce a long cyan line (#00FFFF) passing through one star, rotating slowly clockwise.
The laser beam hits a second star, and the center of rotation instantly shifts to that star.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: Pivots and Rotation
lecture_lines: A pivot point is the center of rotation.
Rotating a line 180 degrees swaps its sides.
This divides the plane into two distinct halves.
animations: Focus on one yellow star (#FFFF00) [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/star.svg] as the center of a rotating white line (#FFFFFF).
Color the regions on either side of the rotating line in light magenta (#FF00FF, opacity 0.2) and light green (#00FF00, opacity 0.2).
Rotate the line 180 degrees and show the magenta and green regions swapping positions as the line flips.

section_3.title: The Core Rule: The Hand-off
lecture_lines: The laser rotates around its current pivot point.
It continues until it hits another star.
Instantly, that new star becomes the pivot.
The rotation continues from this new center.
This "hand-off" creates the windmill motion.
animations: Show a cyan line (#00FFFF) rotating clockwise around a yellow pivot star A (#FFFF00).
The line rotates until it makes contact with a white star B (#FFFFFF).
Star B flashes and turns yellow (#FFFF00) while Star A turns white (#FFFFFF), indicating the pivot has changed.
The cyan line continues rotating clockwise, now using Star B as its center of rotation.
Repeat the sequence: the line hits a third star C, which then becomes the new yellow pivot star.

section_4.title: The Invariant Property: The Balancing Act
lecture_lines: Watch the stars on one side of the line.
As the line rotates, stars stay on their side.
During a hand-off, the count remains the same.
This invariant property is the key to the proof.
No matter the pivot, the balance never changes.
animations: Highlight all stars currently to the left of the rotating laser in orange (#FFA500).
As the laser rotates towards star B, show that star B is the next point the beam will encounter.
The line sweeps through star B; stars already on the left remain on the left.
After the pivot shift to star B, show that the set of orange stars on the left has not changed.
Display a counter 'Stars on Left: n' at the top, which stays constant during the pivot hand-off.

section_5.title: Step-by-Step Visualization (3-Point Case)
lecture_lines: Start with the laser pivoting at Point A.
It rotates and hits Point B, its new pivot.
Next, it hits Point C and continues spinning.
After 180 degrees, the line returns to Point A.
Notice how the sides have now completely swapped.
animations: Draw three stars A, B, and C in a triangular formation on the plane.
The laser starts at star A, rotates clockwise, and 'hands off' the pivot to star B.
The laser rotates from star B, hits star C, and then rotates from star C back to star A.
Show the laser line returning to its original horizontal orientation after a total rotation of 180 degrees.
Draw a faint grey dotted path (#555555) connecting A, B, and C to show the pivot's movement.

section_6.title: Conclusion: The Infinite Loop
lecture_lines: The invariant side-count ensures a repeating cycle.
With finite stars, the windmill hits every point.
Geometry transforms a simple rule into an infinite dance.
animations: Accelerate the animation, showing the laser [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/laser.svg] quickly cycling through various stars [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/star.svg] in the set.

As the laser [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/laser.svg] hits each star [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/star.svg], it briefly glows to show it has been part of the windmill process.
Fade out the points and line to leave behind a complex, symmetric pattern of the line's history.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "The Hook: Meet Milly the Laser Robot"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Meet Milly, a robot in a field of stars.",
            "She holds a laser beam that rotates clockwise.",
            "Today, we explore how this beam moves."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        STAR_COLOR = WHITE
        LASER_COLOR = TEAL
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = YELLOW
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Create stars representing a field
        # Grid positions for stars: C3 (Pivot 1), D4 (Pivot 2), B4, E3, C5, D2, B5
        # L003: 1-column buffer (Col 2+), avoid Col 6 and Row F
        star_positions = ["C3", "D4", "B4", "E3", "C5", "D2", "B5"]
        stars = VGroup(*[Dot(color=STAR_COLOR, radius=0.08) for _ in star_positions])
        for star, pos in zip(stars, star_positions):
            self.place_at_grid(star, pos)
            
        # Label for Milly at pivot 1 (C3)
        # L003: Label in Col 2, Target in Col 3 (C2 vs C3)
        milly_label = Text("Milly", font_size=24, color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(milly_label, "C2", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(STAR_COLOR),
            FadeIn(stars, lag_ratio=0.1),
            Write(milly_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # She holds a laser beam that rotates clockwise.
        # Pivot initially on star at C3
        pivot_data = {"pos": stars[0].get_center()}
        
        # Define the laser with an updater (L010)
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        laser = Line(color=LASER_COLOR, stroke_width=3)
        
        def update_laser(m):
            theta = angle_tracker.get_value()
            p = pivot_data["pos"]
            length = 10 # Long enough to span the 6x6 grid
            direction = np.array([np.cos(theta), np.sin(theta), 0])
            # L008: Avoid missing methods, set_points_by_ends is robust for Line
            m.set_points_by_ends(p - direction * length/2, p + direction * length/2)
            
        laser.add_updater(update_laser)
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(LASER_COLOR),
            Create(laser),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        
        # Initial clockwise rotation
        # Star 1 (C3) is at (2.5, 0.2), Star 2 (D4) is at (3.5, -0.8)
        # Vector is (1, -1), angle is -45 degrees
        target_angle_1 = -45 * DEGREES
        
        self.play(
            angle_tracker.animate.set_value(target_angle_1),
            run_time=3,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Today, we explore how this beam moves.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR))
        
        # Highlight the hit star (L004: Indicate)
        self.play(Indicate(stars[1], color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR, scale_factor=1.5))
        
        # Shift pivot to star 2 (D4)
        pivot_data["pos"] = stars[1].get_center()
        
        # Move label to new pivot position D4 (label at D3)
        # Using grid coordinate for movement (L003 Area-Positioning Rule)
        target_label_pos = self.grid["D3"]
        
        self.play(
            milly_label.animate.move_to(target_label_pos),
            angle_tracker.animate.set_value(target_angle_1 - 90 * DEGREES),
            run_time=4,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # White line passing through the pivot
        rotating_line = Line(LEFT * 3.5, RIGHT * 3.5, color=COLOR_LINE, stroke_width=4)
        rotating_line.move_to(pivot.get_center())
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(pivot),
            FadeIn(pivot_label),
            Create(rotating_line)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        # Create regions (half-planes)

        self.play(

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data
        lecture_lines = [
            "The invariant side-count ensures a repeating cycle.",
            "With finite stars, the windmill hits every point.",
            "Geometry transforms a simple rule into an infinite dance."
        ]
        
        # Setup
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: The Infinite Loop", lecture_lines)
        
        # Visual elements
        # Lesson L003: Reserving Row A, using columns 2-5 to avoid lecture notes and clipping.
        stars_pos = ["B3", "C2", "D2", "E3", "E5", "D5", "C5"]
        stars = VGroup()
        for pos in stars_pos:
            star = Star(color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.8)
            self.place_at_grid(star, pos, scale_factor=0.15)
            stars.add(star)
            
        pivot_star = Star(color=WHITE, fill_opacity=1)
        self.place_at_grid(pivot_star, "C4", scale_factor=0.2)
        pivot_origin = self.grid["C4"]
        
        # Laser line
        # Initial line definition
        laser = Line(LEFT * 3.5, RIGHT * 3.5, color=RED, stroke_width=3)
        laser.move_to(pivot_origin)
        
        # Tracking variables
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Lesson L008: Use persistent mobjects and updaters for render stability
        def update_laser(m):
            angle = angle_tracker.get_value()
            direction = np.array([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0])
            m.set_points_by_ends(pivot_origin - 3.5 * direction, pivot_origin + 3.5 * direction)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "The invariant side-count ensures a repeating cycle."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Lesson L011: Animation entry via FadeIn/Create
        self.play(FadeIn(stars), FadeIn(pivot_star))
        self.play(Create(laser))
        
        laser.add_updater(update_laser)
        
        # Accelerate rotation to show cycle speed
        self.play(
            angle_tracker.animate.set_value(4 * PI),
            run_time=4,
            rate_func=rate_functions.ease_in_sine
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "With finite stars, the windmill hits every point."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Stars glow as laser "hits" them
        # Generate sequential animations for each star
        star_animations = []
        for i in range(len(stars)):
            star_animations.append(
                Succession(
                    Wait(i * 0.4),
                    stars[i].animate.scale(1.5).set_color(WHITE),
                    stars[i].animate.scale(1/1.5).set_color(YELLOW)
                )
            )

        self.play(
            angle_tracker.animate.set_value(8 * PI),
            *star_animations,
            run_time=4,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Geometry transforms a simple rule into an infinite dance."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Create a history trail of the line to leave a "flower-like" pattern
        history = VGroup()
        for i in range(36):
            angle = i * (2 * PI / 36)
            # Cardioid-like offset to create a symmetric flower pattern (as per storyboard)
            offset_mag = 0.3 * np.sin(3 * angle) 
            offset = offset_mag * np.array([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0])
            
            # Lesson L015: Keep trail lines thin and low-opacity to avoid clutter
            l = Line(LEFT * 3.5, RIGHT * 3.5, color=RED, stroke_width=0.8, stroke_opacity=0.15)
            l.rotate(angle)
            l.move_to(pivot_origin + offset)
            history.add(l)
            
        self.play(
            FadeIn(history, lag_ratio=0.05),
            stars.animate.set_fill_opacity(0.1),
            pivot_star.animate.set_fill_opacity(0.1),
            laser.animate.set_stroke_opacity(0.05),
            run_time=5
        )
        
        self.wait(3)

outline.title: The Invariant Property: The Balancing Act
outline.content: Introduce the 'Aha!' moment: the 'Number of Points on One Side' property. Explain that as the line rotates and changes pivots, the number of points on the left side of the line remains constant.
outline.example: Imagine 5 sheep in a field. If the laser line starts with 2 sheep on its left, no matter how many times it 'hits' a new sheep and changes pivots, there will always be exactly 2 sheep on the left side.

storyboard.title: The Invariant Property: The Balancing Act
lecture_lines: Watch the stars on one side of the line.
As the line rotates, stars stay on their side.
During a hand-off, the count remains the same.
This invariant property is the key to the proof.
No matter the pivot, the balance never changes.
animations: Highlight all stars currently to the left of the rotating laser in orange (#FFA500).
As the laser rotates towards star B, show that star B is the next point the beam will encounter.
The line sweeps through star B; stars already on the left remain on the left.
After the pivot shift to star B, show that the set of orange stars on the left has not changed.
Display a counter 'Stars on Left: n' at the top, which stays constant during the pivot hand-off.

outline.title: The Core Rule: The Hand-off
outline.content: Define the 'Windmill' movement rule. A line rotates around a pivot point until it hits another point in the set. At that exact moment, the hit point becomes the new pivot, and the rotation continues.
outline.example: An animation of a rotating baton. As soon as the tip of the baton touches a bystander, that person grabs the center and the baton starts spinning around their hand instead.

storyboard.title: The Core Rule: The Hand-off
lecture_lines: The laser rotates around its current pivot point.
It continues until it hits another star.
Instantly, that new star becomes the pivot.
The rotation continues from this new center.
This "hand-off" creates the windmill motion.
animations: Show a cyan line (#00FFFF) rotating clockwise around a yellow pivot star A (#FFFF00).
The line rotates until it makes contact with a white star B (#FFFFFF).
Star B flashes and turns yellow (#FFFF00) while Star A turns white (#FFFFFF), indicating the pivot has changed.
The cyan line continues rotating clockwise, now using Star B as its center of rotation.
Repeat the sequence: the line hits a third star C, which then becomes the new yellow pivot star.

outline.content: Walk through a full 180-degree rotation cycle using a simple triangle of points to show how the pivot moves and how the line returns to its original orientation.

        )

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]

        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data
        lecture_lines = [
            "The invariant side-count ensures a repeating cycle.",
            "With finite stars, the windmill hits every point.",
            "Geometry transforms a simple rule into an infinite dance."
        ]
        
        # Setup
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: The Infinite Loop", lecture_lines)
        
        # Assets - Lesson L009: Using designated assets
        laser_path = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/laser.svg"
        star_path = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/star.svg"

        # Stars layout - Using Col 4 and 5 to avoid lecture notes (L003)
        # Pivot point set to C5 (Issue 37, 38)
        stars_pos = ["B4", "B5", "D4", "D5", "C4", "E4"]
        
        stars = VGroup()
        for pos in stars_pos:
            # SVGMobject for star as per storyboard
            star = SVGMobject(star_path).set_color(YELLOW).set_fill(YELLOW, opacity=0.8)
            self.place_at_grid(star, pos, scale_factor=0.2)
            stars.add(star)
            
        pivot_star = SVGMobject(star_path).set_color(WHITE).set_fill(WHITE, opacity=1)
        self.place_at_grid(pivot_star, "C5", scale_factor=0.15) # Scale factor as per Issue 37
        pivot_origin = self.grid["C5"]
        
        # Laser line as SVGMobject - Stretched to form a beam
        laser = SVGMobject(laser_path).set_color(RED)
        laser.stretch_to_fit_width(3.0)
        laser.stretch_to_fit_height(0.05)
        laser.move_to(pivot_origin)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "The invariant side-count ensures a repeating cycle."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # L011: Entry animations
        self.play(FadeIn(stars), FadeIn(pivot_star))
        self.play(Create(laser))
        
        # Use Rotate for performance and stability over updaters (L024)
        self.play(
            Rotate(laser, angle=2 * PI, about_point=pivot_origin),
            run_time=2,
            rate_func=rate_functions.ease_in_out_sine
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "With finite stars, the windmill hits every point."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Storyboard: Hit each star, making it glow
        # L004: Using Indicate. L024: Simpler parallel animations to prevent timeout.
        self.play(
            Rotate(laser, angle=2 * PI, about_point=pivot_origin),
            LaggedStart(
                *[Indicate(s, color=WHITE, scale_factor=1.2) for s in stars],
                lag_ratio=0.15
            ),
            run_time=2.5,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Geometry transforms a simple rule into an infinite dance."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Storyboard: Fade out points and line to leave behind a history pattern
        # L024: Minimal count of history elements to ensure render budget.
        history = VGroup()
        for i in range(8):
            angle = i * (PI / 4)
            l = Line(LEFT * 1.5, RIGHT * 1.5, color=RED, stroke_width=0.5, stroke_opacity=0.3)
            l.rotate(angle)
            l.move_to(pivot_origin)
            history.add(l)
            
        self.play(
            FadeIn(history, lag_ratio=0.05),
            stars.animate.set_fill_opacity(0.1),
            pivot_star.animate.set_fill_opacity(0.1),
            laser.animate.set_stroke_opacity(0.1).set_fill_opacity(0.1),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        self.wait(1)
